texts: On day 631 of Year 2, mire-essence formed in the three cauldrons by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in three clay vessels.
Keepers drew the stored mire-essence at sundown.
Keepers lit the lanterns of the East Row with the stored mire-essence at sundown.
Tessa Brae collected forty of the fallen feathers at the base of the cliff in the morning.
Tessa Brae added the feathers to the feather bin.
Bevin Coombe took feathers from the feather bin.
Bevin Coombe scattered the ground feathers around the Stilllight Lantern at sundown.
The ground feathers warded the Stilllight Lantern against wraiths.
No wraith approached the Stilllight Lantern that night.

q1_issues.issue: "that night" emits only the day-part symbol night; the anaphoric-temporal-NP rule requires copying the antecedent's day-level terms — (Day 631) and (Year 2) are stated and known, so they should have been propagated onto the approach event.

q2_gaps: an ordinal day-of-year in a non-Gregorian calendar ("day 631 of Year 2") — the Time term inventory supplies only (Day <n>) for a calendar day-of-month, so a day-of-year reading is indistinguishable from a day-of-month one
review.notes: The "forty of the fallen feathers" partitive (superset + SubsetOf subset + Cardinality + distributed "fallen" rule), the "by evening" TimeAtMost deadline, and the strength-0 rule plus QuantifierPhrase for "No wraith approached" all follow the instruction set exactly. "the lanterns of the East Row" taking Possession rather than PartOf is a defensible reading of the one genitive test, though the part/whole branch looks the closer fit.

issues.reason: The Time section's term-propagation rule is mandatory — 'that evening / day / night' copies the antecedent event's day-level terms (Weekday / Day / Month / Year, whichever are stated) plus the day-part symbol — and (Day 631) and (Year 2) are stated on the forming event, so emitting the day-part alone violates it.

gaps_confirmed: 'day 631 of Year 2' — (Day <n>) is the instruction set's day-of-month slot, so a day-of-year reading in a non-Gregorian calendar is stored indistinguishably from a day-of-month one
new_gaps: whether a transitive predicate over a definite or counted plural OBJECT hands the predication to each member is unspecified: the per-member (PartOf $x <group>) rule is stated for plural SUBJECTS (Cardinality, Quantifiers) and for a resultative's flat half, leaving 'lit the lanterns of the East Row', 'collected forty of the fallen feathers' and 'ground the feathers' with no settled per-member form
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form propagates the antecedent's stated day-level terms into the rule's conclusion — (Time (sk_approach $x) (Day 631)) and (Time (sk_approach $x) (Year 2)) beside (Time (sk_approach $x) night) — the same shape the instruction set gives for 'that evening' after a dated antecedent.
adjudication.notes: The rest of the parse is close: the 'forty of the fallen feathers' partitive with its distributed 'fallen' rule, the 'by evening' TimeAtMost deadline, event-only Location for the forming and the storing, the preposition-named Around / Against obliques, and the strength-0 rule plus QuantifierPhrase for 'No wraith approached'. 'the lanterns of the East Row' as Possession rather than PartOf is defensible under the genitive's single part/whole test, so it would not fail the parse on its own.
